name: og-06-chemistry-to-heredity
title: Chemistry to heredity (Campaign VI)
question: Does inherited state improve persistence/throughput — comparing RNA-like, peptide-assisted, compositional and hybrid heredity — rather than template replication in isolation? (Do NOT presume RNA.)
hypothesis: At least one heredity module raises lineage persistence + information retention above its non-heritable control under a feasible resource budget; the winner is not assumed a priori.
objective: Introduce competing heredity modules and test whether inherited state improves persistence under feasible budgets.
proposed_mechanisms: J: polymers, information and heredity (as competing modules)

conditions.name: reproducibility
conditions.expr: solver and db and seed and scenario recorded

contract.note: bigraph-schema typed ports (_type/_units/bounds) + conservation predicates; the composite built for this study must declare a ProcessContract matching this face (audited via the workbench §Contract panel).

behavior_tests.name: inheritance-beats-noninheritance
behavior_tests.description: Heritable systems outperform their non-heritable controls.

measure.detail: persistence/throughput with vs without inherited state

behavior_tests.name: heredity-modules-compared
behavior_tests.description: At least two heredity modules evaluated head-to-head.

behavior_tests.name: replication-feasible-budget
behavior_tests.description: Demonstrated under feasible resource budgets, not idealized.

literature_anchors.expectation: Mineral/CO-driven peptide formation at 100 C, pH 7-10
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Not yet measurable — module processes not built

key_assumptions: Treat informational chemistry as a branch point; do not presume a viable RNA replication mechanism.
expert_questions: Which heredity modules to prioritize first: RNA-world, peptide-first, compositional, or mineral-surface templating?
